skill.card_work.body.content:
# Work with cards

Follow this procedure when creating, running, or owning a Soulstream card. This skill defines card creation, assignee and member roles, state transitions, questions and answers, summaries, and reports. Other rules and skills reference it for shared procedures and describe their own procedures separately. The shared `workflow.md` gives the rules every session needs and tells sessions when to read this skill. Atom knowledge cards and cards in other services are outside its scope.

## Give the user a short status and a result to check

The card gives the user three things. Show the current situation in one line, the results and evidence to check, and whether the card is complete. Keep progress history, technical details, designs, delegation briefs, and session history in notes and the sessions tab. The user can comment on an item when it needs a correction. The comment goes to the assignee. There is no rejection step.

## Size a card and attach sessions

- A card is one request the user can confirm as done in a single decision. Split implementation by repository or PR across work sessions. If the checklist keeps growing across distinct deliverables, reconsider the card's scope.
- A session has one of two relationships to a card.
  - **Assignee** (`assignee.kind = session`, `assignee_session_id`). This session owns the card. Each card has one assignee session and each session owns at most one card. Completed and canceled cards count. Archived cards are excluded. The dispatcher launches the assignee for a card the user assigns through the input or queue. A session is the assignee when its context has `card.role` set to `assignee` or when it creates a card and assigns itself.
  - **Member** (`sessions.card_id`). The assignee attaches a work session to handle part of the work. It belongs to exactly one card and appears in the card's sessions list. Its context has `card.role` set to `member`.
- Only the assignee uses `set_card_items`, `add_card_item`, `report_card_item`, `update_card_now`, `add_card_note`, `update_card_brief`, `request_card_review`, `ask_card_question`, `withdraw_card_question`, and `add_card_comment`. Members report results and questions to the session that delegated the work. A card question goes to the user when the assignee needs the user's decision.

## Assignee responsibilities

1. Before starting, use `get_card` to read the request, checklist, status summary, handoff summary, questions, comments, notes, and linked sessions. If the initial prompt lists other active card sessions, check for work on the same repository or files. If work overlaps, pause and ask with `ask_card_question`.
2. Follow "Start card work explicitly". Set a checklist with `set_card_items` when the card has none. Use `update_card_now` when the situation changes, `add_card_note` for progress and technical details, and `update_card_brief` for what the next session needs to know.
3. As you finish each item, attach a one-line result and evidence with `report_card_item`. Resolve outstanding work before calling `request_card_review`. Use `ask` to give the user one line on what to check. For recurring cards, follow "Complete recurring cards as the assignee". Review delegated work before summarizing it on the checklist.
4. When you need the user's decision, call `ask_card_question(card_id, title, text, options)` and end the turn. The question appears immediately on the user's "Current reports" board. The board records the selected option as the card answer. Follow "Write card questions". The server resumes the same session when an answer arrives. Use `ask_card_question` for this step. Skip `AskUserQuestion`. If a conversation or comment resolves an open question, withdraw it with `withdraw_card_question(card_id, question_id, reason)` and explain the decision in `reason`.
5. Record user instructions from conversation as a user summary. Follow "Keep user statements and agent replies distinct" and keep your own answers and decisions separate.
6. Keep the card in progress while waiting for delegated work. Ending a turn alone says nothing about completion, missing results, or blockers. Record results and request review when the work finishes.
7. If work resumes after a usage limit interrupts it, make a WIP commit first.
8. For a correction received by comment or in conversation, follow "Reply on the card that received the comment". Reopen the card, mark the item as in progress, and update the status summary before working.
9. Triage out-of-scope findings. Fix qualifying defects in the area this card changes. Drop findings that do not merit a fix. Send the remaining findings to the PAS as described below and keep them off the card.

## Write card questions

Give enough context for someone who has not seen the conversation to answer from the question alone. The PAS board, card detail, iPhone, iPad, and card app use the fields from `ask_card_question` to render the title, context, material to review, and options.

1. Ask for one decision per question. When decisions depend on each other, start with the first one. For several decisions of the same kind, such as terminology, ask in groups of three or four and show the current and proposed values in a table. Avoid an overall approval question or a single question for the entire list. Recurring card proposals are the exception.
2. Put the decision in one line of `title` (up to 40 characters). It appears at the top of the question and in the notification title, "Confirmation requested: Title" or "Request: Title".
3. Use about 400 characters in `text` for context, up to 1,200. Explain in plain language what happened, why the decision is needed now, how urgent it is, and what you recommend and why. Keep the context even if it makes the question longer. Phone notifications show only the first 100 characters of the body. Lead with the point. Use names the user knows from the UI. Avoid function, file, or setting names and labels invented during work, such as "Option A" or "cover".
4. Give one to three `options` as `{label, description, recommended}`. Use a short `label` (up to 12 characters) and a `description` that explains what choosing it does (up to 80 characters). Set `recommended: true` on only one option. The UI labels it "Recommended". Include options whose consequences you can explain in one line. Keep option descriptions out of `text`.
5. Leave "Other" out of the options. The screen already offers "Write an answer" for a free-text answer and "Ask a follow-up".
6. When the user must take an action, such as signing in, updating, or trying a control, set `kind: "request"` and omit `options`. Put the steps in a numbered list in `text`. The UI shows a "Card request" chip and an "I did it" button. The server records the `했어` (shown as "I did it") answer.
7. When the user needs to choose based on a mockup or image, add up to four images in `attachments`, using the same format as checklist evidence. The user can enlarge them from the question. For consent to a proposal, attach the mockup to the checklist item as well. See "Mockups for user consent".
8. Check the question history and handoff summary before asking. The user may have decided already.
9. To update an open question, pass its `question_id` and the full updated content to `ask_card_question`. The question updates in place, shows "Edited at {{time}}", and sends no new notification.
10. Answers and thread messages go to the current assignee, or to the session that created the question if there is no assignee.
    - A selected option or text answer arrives in a `[카드 질문 답변]` message. A selection can include an additional note.
    - A follow-up question arrives in a `[카드 질문 되묻기]` message. The question stays open. Reply using `add_card_comment` with `mode: "reply"` and `question_id`. Send one reply per user message, up to 1,200 characters. If the user asks because the question lacked information, update it in place as in step 9.
    - An addition after an answer arrives in a `[카드 질문 덧붙임]` message. The question stays closed. Apply the user's clarification and use the same reply format if a reply is needed.
    - A thread reply leaves the question and card state as they are.
    - If the user speaks in a regular comment or conversation outside the question, the server closes the question. Reply in a comment, then ask again with revised wording if needed. Reflect what the user said.

## Cards initiated by a PAS

- The server mirrors cards that a persistent agent session (PAS) creates, runs, or sends follow-up instructions to, including new cards created when their assignees divide the work. The cards appear on the user's "Current reports" board. Review and blocked states add a card entry. An open question adds a question entry. A return to running or awaiting verification, or completion, removes the card entry. Putting a card on hold removes all of its entries. Taking it off hold restores entries for open questions, or a card entry if the card is in review or blocked and there are no open questions.
- The card entry shows the status summary. When the user has the turn, it shows `ask`. Otherwise it shows the current status line. Write `ask` in `request_card_review` and the blocked status in `update_card_now` so the user can see what to check or what is blocked from that line alone.
- Record results on the card and its status summary. This replaces old handoff instructions that named a reporting PAS and requested a report via `send_message_to_session`. Use `ask_card_question` for user decisions. Send only out-of-scope findings directly to the PAS.
- When splitting work into a new card, leave the previous PAS reporting destination out of the handoff.

## Send out-of-scope findings to the PAS

Send qualifying findings directly to the PAS, which decides whether to create a card. Keep them out of the closing note and the user's next action.

- A finding is out of scope when its problem, repair, or follow-up lies beyond the card's request and checklist. The same rule applies to observations, deferred follow-ups, requests for a separate card, and failures outside the change.
- Apply two checks before sending.
  1. A defect in a screen, window, app area, file, component, or feature the card changes belongs to the current card. This applies to preexisting defects and defects a work session reported outside the original spec. Use the threshold below. For UI work, gather the relevant defects in the first review and fix them together. Report the fixes under the closest checklist item.
  2. Send only findings that meet the threshold for follow-up work in `proportional-engineering.md`. Group findings below the threshold as "Omitted" in the closing note with a one-line reason.
- Keep out-of-scope findings out of notes, both status summary fields, checklist results and caveats, handoffs, comments, card questions, and review requests. The handoff exception below applies only if sending fails. Keep `caveat` for parts of the card's own result you could not verify.
- Apply the same two checks to findings and review issues raised by work sessions. Handle qualifying defects within the area this card changes and send only the rest.
- Send to the main PAS. Call `list_persistent_sessions()` and choose "Seo Soyoung persistent session" under the "Seo Soyoung (PAS)" agent. Pass its full `session_id` to `send_message_to_session(target_session_id, message)`. See the section on finding a persistent session in `soulstream-session`. A session in `completed` wakes when it receives the message. Use a different work PAS when the request, handoff, or follow-up names one for these findings.
- Combine findings in one message before requesting review. Send a finding immediately if it is breaking the user's current work.
- If sending returns `ok:false`, read `error` and use the appropriate recovery below. Keep the findings out of the status summary, questions, and review request.
  - `session-data host get failed` or `target owner lookup failed`. Looking up the PAS node timed out. A large PAS history can cause the same failure on a retry from another node. Route the Soulstream issue to the PAS and start a relay on the PAS node, using the `node_id` from `list_persistent_sessions`. Call `create_remote_agent_session(node_id: PAS node, agent_id: "seosoyoung" or the node's default profile, an available lightweight preset, notify_completion: true)`. Include the complete message and these instructions in the prompt. Load `send_message_to_session`. Call it once with the full PAS session ID as `target_session_id` and the supplied text verbatim as `message`. Return the result as one line of JSON. A completion result of `{"ok":true,…}` confirms delivery.
  - Use a preset outside the sandbox for the relay, such as a preset named with the `trusted` marker or a `claude-opus` preset. A sandboxed preset such as `claude-haiku` cannot send to sessions outside its caller chain and receives `MCP_POLICY_DENIED: message-recipient`. If the assignee receives this error, it is running in the sandbox. Use the handoff fallback because the sandbox also blocks remote session creation.
  - If the session cannot be found, resolve the full ID again with `list_persistent_sessions` and retry once.
  - If the relay fails or cannot start, add `## Findings not delivered to the PAS` to the end of the handoff summary and paste the message verbatim. Keep the delivery issue out of the notes, status summary, and review request. The PAS picks up this section when processing the review notification and reading the handoff. See `pas-role.md`.
- Use the following message format. Give the PAS enough context to decide without reading this conversation.

```
[Separate issue] #<card number> <card title>
1. Finding: one or two sentences
   Evidence: file and line, screen, reproduction conditions, session ID
   Impact: who experiences what and when
   Urgency: affecting the user now / can wait
   Why this card leaves it separate: another repository, assignee, node, screen, or deliverable
   Suggested next step: link to an existing card or create one, if applicable
```

- After sending, continue without waiting for a response or recording delivery on the card. The PAS decides whether to append the finding to an existing card, create a card, or drop it. When it sends a finding back, it comes as a follow-up instruction. Explain why the issue belongs outside the card because the PAS returns findings that touch the area the card changes. If a follow-up arrives after review or completion, reopen and make the correction in the same order as for a card comment. The follow-up is recorded as a statement. If there is no suitable item, use `add_card_item` with `from_comment_id` pointing to that record.
- Create or run new cards only to divide work the user requested. The PAS handles cards for out-of-scope findings.

## Resolve outstanding work before requesting review

Users look at the checklist and status summary when a card awaits review. Work left only in a closing note or under "If reopened" in the handoff has no owner. That includes pending deployments left because approval would restart a node runtime and review findings left on record without a decision.

1. Before calling `request_card_review`, collect all remaining work. Look through the closing note, handoff, and work-session reports for "Remaining work", "If reopened", "Later", "Pending", "For the record", and "Hand off to the user". Include non-blocking review findings and unapproved deployments.
2. Decide what to do with each item. Recording it alone leaves it open.
   - Finish it on this card. Use this option for work that affects the card's deliverable. Approve and finish pending deployments for this card on any node. Soulstream updates without downtime, so a node runtime restart by itself is no reason to leave a deployment pending. If another approval or a newer commit absorbed the pending deployment, check the node's deployment history for this commit and record the result on the checklist.
   - Send a finding about a separate deliverable to the PAS if it meets the follow-up threshold in `proportional-engineering.md`. Follow "Send out-of-scope findings to the PAS" and keep it off the card.
   - Omit work below the same follow-up threshold. Record "Omitted" and the reason in one line in the closing note. A defect in the area this card changes needs a reason beyond being outside the original request. You can group several non-blocking review findings on one line. Leaving a finding on record is insufficient.
3. Keep responsibility for operational checks you cannot run yet, such as live use after deployment, a scheduled build result, or a rare display condition. If you can check later, set awaiting verification with `wake_at` and `waiting_for` and request review after you wake and verify. If you cannot check, for example because the condition has not occurred in production or no real device is available, record the gap in the item's `caveat` and request review.
4. When requesting review, leave only the user's review under remaining work in the handoff. If the user asks for a correction, reopen the card based on that instruction.
5. If a decision belongs to the user, use `ask_card_question` before requesting review. Examples include choices of direction or scope, paid calls costing at least $1, and changes that are hard to reverse.
6. Before requesting review, update the linked atom project card if you investigated a repository for the first time, established an architecture or schema, changed build or verification commands, or found a recurring pitfall.

When the PAS receives a review notification, it reads the checklist, handoff, and last closing note. It sends unhandled work back to the assignee. See `pas-role.md`. For incidental repair cards that the user did not request, the PAS can complete the card without user review when the fix is clear, needs no user decision, and has no outstanding work. The user may never see the review request's `ask` on such cards. Use a card question for anything they need to decide or see.

## Complete recurring cards as the assignee

- This applies to cards created by recurring jobs, such as a daily work review or a morning reminder, whose prompts point to this section. It also applies to summary cards created automatically from external requests, such as a digest of material sent by an external tool.
- Attach results, evidence, and caveats to the checklist. Set `set_card_status(status: done)` yourself and skip `request_card_review`.
- Use `ask_card_question` only for proposals or decisions that require the user. Bundle multiple proposals in one question with options. Apply the answer before completing the card.
- If failure or interruption prevented a result, leave the card blocked and record the reason in the notes.

## Member work sessions

- Send questions and deliverables to the delegating session. Pause when you need an answer. Leave card tools to the assignee. See `code-delegation.md`.
- The assignee reviews the report and summarizes it as a checklist result with evidence.
- List out-of-scope findings separately in your report and leave them for the assignee to triage and send to the PAS.

## Tool fields and the card UI

The tools accept structured fields. The server enforces lengths, counts, and identifiers. Use the write arguments below. The read response from `get_card` uses `now.text` and `body` for notes and comments.

| Field | Tool | What to write |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Checklist | `set_card_items`, `add_card_item` (`title`, `from_comment_id`), `report_card_item` (`item_id`, `state`: doing/done/dropped, `result`, `evidence`, `caveat`) | One result the user can check per item, with evidence such as screenshots or links and anything you could not verify |
| Status summary | `update_card_now` (`now`, `turn`: agent/user/outside, `ask`) | The current situation in one line and whose turn it is |
| Notes | `add_card_note` (`text`) | Progress, technical details, and identifiers for other agents |
| Handoff summary | `update_card_brief` | What the next session should read first, shown at the top of the notes tab |
| Comments | `add_card_comment` (`text`, `mode`: reply/spoken, `question_id`) | Replies to the user, with `question_id` for question threads, and records of what the user said in conversation |

- Pass `expected_version` (the current card `version`) and `idempotency_key` to `set_card_status` and `start_card_work`. Wait for a write such as `update_card_brief` or `set_card_items` to return the new `version` before calling them. Sending writes together can cause a version conflict.
- For `card_id`, use the full UUID from `<soulstream_session>.card.id` or `get_card`, or a card number prefixed with `#`, such as `#12`. Only `get_card` accepts a bare numeric string such as `"12"`. Other card tools return `CARD_NOT_FOUND`.
- At the start, use `set_card_items` to turn the request into results. Each item should name one result the user can verify on screen or in the deliverable and confirm as done. Keep work steps, PRs, and verification procedures out of the checklist.
- Document per-screen and per-device details in the relevant result and its evidence. Give separate checklist items to distinct results. If six items are awaiting confirmation and the tool accepts no more, wait for the user to confirm them.
- Set `state: doing` on `report_card_item` when you start an item, including a correction requested in a comment. Attach a one-line result and evidence when finished. Add an item with `add_card_item` only for a new user instruction and link the user's statement. Preserve user-confirmed items unless you have a reason to change them.
- Keep progress, technical details, and handoff information in the notes. Check the status summary before ending the turn.
- The checklist is for results the user can verify. Only the user checks off items. Divide the work itself among work sessions.

### Write a result the user can verify

- Describe what changed in plain language in one line. For example, write that selecting "Done" returns the user to the previous list. Put function and file names, commit IDs, and test counts in the notes.
- Attach evidence the user can inspect, such as a real screenshot, an accessible page, or an output file. Use links for long documents. Staged images and example screens do not count as evidence.
- Link to a folder Markdown document with a relative URL such as `{type: "link", label, url: "/?document=<document.id>"}`. Use `document.id` returned by `create_markdown_document` rather than `boardItem.id`. Start the URL with `/`. An absolute `http://` URL will not work here.
- Record any unverified scope, such as real devices or production rollout, in `caveat`. Describe incomplete work as incomplete.
- For server work without a UI, describe behavior the user can observe. Leave evidence empty when there is nothing to attach.
- Put the current situation in plain language in the status summary. If it is the user's turn, tell them what to check in one line.
- Name the actual items in results, caveats, and reports. For example, say "Change spelling A to B" instead of giving only the number of suspect spellings. Resolve uncertain values using existing usage, the card's principles, and related decisions. Record your evidence.

### Attach screenshots to the checklist item

- For UI work, use `report_card_item` with `evidence` of `type: image` to attach a real screenshot of the change to its item. Put the representative screenshot first and briefly identify the screen and platform. Make it available on the card itself.
- Register the file with `register_attachment(local_path, target_scope={type: "card", id: "<full card UUID>"})`. Use the returned `attachment_id` in `report_card_item` evidence (`type: "image"` for images) or in `ask_card_question` attachments. A path outside the caller's workspace, attached worktree, and own `incoming` directory returns `ATTACHMENT_PATH_DENIED`. If the assignee works in a separate workspace, use the `attachment_id` the authoring member registered and reported. A session with an attached worktree registers its files there. Keep local paths such as `/home/...` and `file://` out of evidence and comments. Keep files in authorized storage with their existing permissions.
- If `register_attachment` reports that R2 is unconfigured, use a board Markdown document (`create_markdown_document`) or report a workspace path. If needed, explain how to connect "File storage" under "Records and administration" in Settings.
- Open the card after saving and verify that both the thumbnail and enlarged image load.
- Record any missing real-device verification in `caveat`. A web check covers the web.
- On an older card without checklist items, use `add_card_comment(mode="reply")` with a Markdown image such as `![What the screenshot shows](image URL)`.

### Iterate using visual evidence

- For work judged from images, such as renders or sheets, update checklist evidence at each stage. Put the most recent image first and take down evidence already judged incorrect. Attach the images to the item.
- Wait for the decision before delegating the next stage or merging. If the user asks to redo an input, stop active work that uses the old input.
- Before fixing a problem shown in the user's screenshot, reproduce the same view state, including toggles, hidden objects, and pose, in the actual viewer. Compare the views side by side. Use wireframe or visibility controls to isolate the responsible object before explaining the cause. Judge the fix from a screenshot of the actual viewer.
- Before asking to run something expensive, such as hours of GPU work or a paid call, overlay the evidence image on the input at full size. Attach that image to the card before asking.

### Mockups for user consent

Before asking the user to approve or choose a screen, layout, or design change, attach a mockup to the card. Use a screenshot, render, or comparison image. Reopen the card after saving to verify the attachment is visible. Name the card and say where to find the mockup in the request for consent. Wait until the mockup is available before asking. Label a mockup as a proposal and use separate evidence for implemented results.

### Request and handoff summary

- Quote the user's key sentence or two verbatim in `request`.
- Use `brief` for what the next session needs first. Include decisions, where to find the materials, completed work, and remaining work. Keep full designs and assignments in the work-session prompt and atom.

### Older cards without checklist items

- The report restriction and limits on reply length and count apply to cards with checklist items. Older cards without them still accept `add_card_report` and comments as before.
- When taking over an older card, use `get_card` to confirm it has no checklist, then use `set_card_items` to create items for the remaining request. Leave existing reports and comments where they are.

## Questions, answers, and attribution

All agents writing on Soulstream cards must determine whose statement they are recording and why before choosing a tool.

### Use comments to reply or record a user instruction

- Reply to user comments or record user instructions from conversation. Use notes for progress and technical details, and checklist items for results. If there is no user comment to reply to and the user needs an update, use the status summary and turn.
- Give a short, plain-language answer. Name the relevant object and describe the symptom, changed behavior, or remaining work the user needs to understand.
- Use `item_id` when the reply clearly belongs to an item.
- Follow the attribution rules and summary format below.

### Keep user statements and agent replies distinct

- A comment written directly by the user is already stored verbatim. Keep that original as the record.
- Use `add_card_comment(mode="spoken")` only to record user instructions received in session conversation. The author is the user and the comment records what they said. Begin with **The following summarizes what the user said.** Leave one blank line, then summarize from the user's perspective and in their tone.
- Include only what the user actually said. Keep agent designs, interpretations, approvals, promises, and progress out of the summary. Preserve the user's conditions and distinguish requests from completed work.
- Use `add_card_comment(mode="reply")` for your explanations, decisions, answers, and updates when replying. Keep the user-summary notice and user attribution for user statements. Keep user instruction summaries separate from agent replies.
- The default `spoken` mode supports older records of user instructions. Specify `mode` on new calls. If the tool you have lacks `reply`, report the gap and restore the assignee's supported reply path. Preserve the correct attribution.

Example of a user summary:

> The following summarizes what the user said.
>
> Serve the fonts Soulstream uses as web fonts. Answer card questions in comments on the relevant card.

Example of an agent reply:

> The web app currently specifies font names. I’ll update it to serve the font files.

### Reply on the card that received the comment

User comments arrive at the assignee in a message beginning with `[카드 커멘트]`. It includes the comment body and ID, the target item and its current state, and the card's current state. Decide whether the user asked a question or requested a change.

- **For a question, confirmation, or explanation**, leave a `reply` comment on that card and end the turn. Keep the card and checklist states as they are. If the card was blocked, the server moved it to running and closed open questions when the comment arrived. Return it to blocked after replying if it still has a blocker. Ask again if a closed question is still needed. When the card awaits review, a question calls for a reply alone. Put the answer on the card before any parallel chat update so the user can find it there.
- **For a correction**, follow the same order as at initial assignment. Do these three things before starting.
  1. If the card is in review or done, reopen it as running with `set_card_status` or `start_card_work`. For a blocked card, the server already moved it to running when the comment arrived.
  2. Set `report_card_item(state: doing)` on the referenced item. If the user already confirmed it, explain why it needs reopening in `reopen_reason`. If the comment introduces a new result to check, add an item with `add_card_item` and reference that comment.
  3. Update the status summary with `update_card_now`.

  Then make the change, attach the result and evidence, and request review again. Apply the same procedure to corrections received in session conversation. See "One card per session. Corrections and new work". Keep the original record of an instruction saved on the card. Treat replying and starting work as separate actions.
- If work requires a user decision, ask with `ask_card_question` and wait. Reply to the user's questions in comments.
- Keep routine conversation off the checklist.
- Members pass the reply to the assignee, who answers on the card.
- Check the write response or read the card again to confirm the target card, body, author, and comment type. Prevent agent replies from being delivered back as user input and waking the same session.

## Instructions received in session chat

- If the user directly messages the assignee of a blocked card from the web or app, the server moves the card to running unless a usage limit blocked it. The assignee decides what to do from other states.
- If the user requested more work, record the instruction in a comment on the relevant card and set its state with an authorized tool. Questions, confirmations, and small talk leave card state alone. Touch only relevant cards.
- For one instruction covering several cards, act only on the cards that require work. Resolve an unclear target from the context and card request. Ask the user only if it remains unclear.
- Check the card state at the start and finish. If permissions or server rules reject a transition, report the rejection. On completion, attach results and request review.

## Start card work explicitly

- Confirm which card you will work on and record `running` with the authorized status or start tool. Check that the call succeeded.
- The assignee can make a manual status write from `todo`, `queued`, `blocked`, `running`, `review`, `done`, or `cancelled`, and on an archived card. A restart reason and report are optional.
- Dispatch follows the runtime's execution identity and assignment consumption procedure. A manual status write needs no execution approval. Leave execution identities to the runtime.
- Reuse the same `idempotency_key` when resending a request. Read the latest card to resolve concurrent update conflicts.
- For a direct conversation, select only relevant cards. Leave status alone for questions and small talk. Members send outcomes to the assignee.
- On completion, attach results and anything you could not verify. If the turn ends while work continues, update the status summary and record progress and remaining work in the notes. Record actual completion separately from permission to change state.

## Card states

The states are `todo` (To do), `queued` (Queued), `blocked` (Blocked), `running` (Running), `awaiting_verification` (Awaiting verification), `review` (Review), `on_hold` (On hold), `done` (Done), and `cancelled` (Canceled). They can be used out of this order.

The generated [card state rules](docs/cards/card-state.md) govern what the server accepts and changes. See the permissions table by actor relationship for who may use each command, and the rules and production call sites table for command behavior. Use the generated document if the summary here differs and update this section accordingly.

Use blocked when you need someone else to unblock the work, for example through a user action, another card or person's result, or external material. Use awaiting verification when you can check again on your own at a set time. Ask for a user decision with `ask_card_question`, which blocks the card. If you finish a stage and need the next instruction, attach the result and leave the card awaiting review. On an unarchived blocked card with an assignee session, a user comment, `dispatch_work` follow-up, or direct message to the assignee returns the card to running unless it is blocked on a usage limit. When the server unblocks it this way, it treats the message as an answer and closes open questions. A manual status change keeps questions open so late answers can arrive. Withdraw questions resolved in conversation or comments with `withdraw_card_question`. A card blocked on questions returns to running when the last open question is answered or withdrawn. Late answers leave completed cards as they are.

Use `awaiting_verification` when the assignee is waiting to check a result, such as real use after a deployment, a measurement at a set time, or a scheduled build. The card must have an assignee session. Call `set_card_status(status: awaiting_verification)` with `wake_at` (ISO 8601 with offset, within seven days) and `waiting_for` (up to 36 characters). The server writes "{What you are waiting for}, check again at {time}" in the status summary. At that time it sends the assignee a `[검증 대기 시각]` message and moves the card to running. When you wake, verify and record the result on the item. If you still need to wait, set a new time. Moving to another state clears both fields. Awaiting verification cards have no PAS board entry and do not count toward running entries. If waking fails, the server blocks the card and sends the usual blocked notice. Use this state for your next check instead of creating a separate one-off job with `create_recurring_job` and `run_at`. A user comment, `dispatch_work` follow-up, or direct message to the assignee returns the card to running as it does from blocked.

If a usage limit ends the assignee's session and resets within five hours, the server wakes the same assignee at reset and moves the card to running. The status summary displays the reset time while the card waits. Replacing the assignee, archiving the card, or moving it out of the limit-blocked state clears the scheduled resume. If you replace the assignee on a card with a scheduled resume and supply no status text, the server writes "The assignee changed, so the scheduled resume was canceled". A later or unknown reset leaves an untimed reservation and triggers no timed wake. Dispatch can continue with the same assignee only when automatic dispatch policy is enabled.

`on_hold` removes the card from the review queue and PAS board without completing or canceling it. The assignee session and worktree remain attached. Find and restore the card from the board's on-hold column. Put a card on hold only at the user's direction. A work instruction on an on-hold card through a comment or `dispatch_work` calls for the same reopening procedure as a correction.

### Change states directly

- The human and assignee agent can move a card between any states. Questions, answers, open questions, reports, restart reasons, and current state are independent of this permission. Only awaiting verification requires an assignee session, `wake_at`, and `waiting_for`.
- If a card is assigned to an agent without an assignee session, a session that agent launched for the card becomes the assignee when it changes state, requests review, or records the start of work. This excludes member sessions started by other sessions on the same card. Only a reply comment can claim assignment through commenting.
- If a card has neither a human nor a session assignee, other agent sessions can move it to to do, queued, on hold, or canceled. The supervising PAS can move an awaiting-review card to done. The PAS uses this permission only for incidental repair cards the user did not request. See `pas-role.md`. Other transitions on an assigned card belong to the authorized assignee or human.
- Agents can record completion or cancellation and reopen done or canceled cards. Archiving is independent of this permission.
- Item results and comments communicate outcomes and context. Attach results before requesting review as the standard workflow. A missing result does not gate a status write. A status-change reason is optional.
- Record the actual situation. Mark work done when it is complete. Preserve actor identity and change history.

### Ending a turn and card progress

- The end of an assignee or member turn does not by itself move the card to `blocked(no_report)`. The assignee assesses the actual situation and reports progress, completion, and whether review is needed.
- Each turn receives current information for this decision. Apply the rules for specific causes such as usage limits. The user can clear a question blocker by changing the state, and the assignee can clear it by explicitly starting work. An unanswered question alone does not put the card back in blocked.

### Status reminders

- Apart from the automatic restart from blocked described above, the system reports mismatches to the assignee with `[카드 상태 확인]` while leaving the state as it is. It sends each reminder type once for the same state.
- The assignee receives a reminder if its turn ended while a member is still running and its card is not running. If the member is working on the card, move it to running. Otherwise leave the card alone.
- The assignee receives a reminder if it and all its work sessions stop while the card is running. If work or the current stage is complete, attach the result and move it to awaiting review. Use `ask_card_question` for a user decision, blocked when someone else must act, and awaiting verification for a check you can make at a set time. Continue if work remains.
- The assignee receives a reminder if a user comment was delivered and its turn ended without a change to the card's state, checklist, status summary, or comments. This happens once per comment. For a correction, update the card and item as in "Reply on the card that received the comment". For a question, leave a reply.
- Keep the state current before a reminder arrives. When ending a turn after delegating, check that the card is running. When no active work remains, use awaiting review or blocked as appropriate. Use awaiting verification when only your own timed check remains.

## One card per session. Corrections and new work

- If the session already owns a card, the server rejects attempts to make it assignee of a new or different card and returns the existing card ID. Follow the procedure below for the type of work.
- **Corrections and follow-up on the same deliverable** belong on the existing card. Record instructions received in chat as user statements on the card. Add a checklist item referencing the comment for a new result to verify. Reopen cards in review or done as running and mark the item in progress. The assignee also receives user comments on completed cards.
- **New work with a separately verifiable outcome** gets a new card. Use `create_card(folder_id, title, request, brief)`. Omit `assignee`, `node_id`, and `model_preset` to inherit the creating session's agent, node, and model. Specify them only when a different assignment makes sense. Use `run=true` to start immediately or `queue=true` to wait in the queue. Leave it as a draft when the user needs to decide. The system starts a new assignee session when the card runs.
- Put the user's original words in `request` and a detailed handoff in `brief`. The new session starts from the card without this conversation. Include context, the original card ID, decisions and exclusions, repositories and documents, completed and remaining work, and completion criteria. After starting, the new assignee uses the handoff to set the checklist and rewrites `brief` as a handoff summary.
- Reuse `idempotency_key` for a retried creation. The original card can proceed independently of the new one.
- When an agent-assigned card has no assignee session, a linked session from the same agent can claim the card by calling `start_card_work` or `set_card_status`. Its own child work sessions cannot claim it.

## Create, run, and queue cards

- The main input starts a session. Use "+ Card" to save a card, or, when a request comes up in conversation, let a session without an assigned card create and own it with `create_card(folder_id, title, request, assignee={kind: session, session_id: current session})`. Persistent sessions follow `pas-role.md`. Sessions that already own a card follow "One card per session. Corrections and new work".
- Create a folder only when the user explicitly requests one. Use the current session folder (`<soulstream_session>.folder`), specifying `folder_id` only for work that belongs elsewhere.
- Use `create_card` to create a draft and `run_card(card_id)` to start a draft, queued, or on-hold card immediately. The system uses the card's node, agent, and model to start an assignee session and move the card to running. It wakes the existing assignee if the card already has one. You can run a card assigned to someone else. Use `run=true` on `create_card` to create and start a card in one call.
- Sessions launched by running a card are independent of the caller. Follow progress on the card because there is no automatic completion report to the caller. The server mirrors cards initiated by a PAS on its board. Use `run_card` to start another card. Starting a session with `create_agent_session` and attaching it as assignee with `transfer_card_assignee` would create a child session and route completion back to its caller.
- Use `queue=true` for work that can wait. The user's PAS starts queued cards when node conditions allow. See `queue-management.md`. Use at most one of `run` and `queue`. If startup confirmation is delayed and the result status is `pending`, call `run_card` again for the same card after a short wait.
- For work that depends on earlier cards, put their prefixed card numbers or UUIDs in `create_card`'s `depends_on` (up to 10 cards) and set `queue=true`. Avoid `run=true` and keep the ordering out of the title. For an unstarted card, use `update_unstarted_card` with the full replacement `depends_on` array. An empty array clears all dependencies. The assignee reads the `선행 카드` (prerequisite cards) line in the startup prompt and uses `get_card` for their results. If a prerequisite is canceled or archived, ask the user whether to replace or remove it, or cancel the dependent card. The server leaves the dependency and dependent card in place.
- To attach a member, call `create_agent_session(card_id=..., caller_session_id=current session)`. This creates membership and leaves card state alone. You can still start sessions without a card for conversation, research, or a quick check.

## Delegate as the assignee

- Split coding work among sessions using an installed profile (`seosoyoung` or `<backend>-default`), or do it in a worktree in this session. See `code-delegation.md`. Include `card_id` for work on a card. Keep parts of the same request on the same card. Put design and assignment details in session prompts and keep `brief` for the handoff. Handle content, operations, and user responses in this session.
- For UI or UX changes, verify the `ui-design` criteria, screenshots and interaction results, and code review before merging.

  ```link
  call: ui-design
  when: When delegating work that changes the UI or receiving its PR and deliverables
  ```
- When a work-session report arrives, verify the evidence as described in `verify-before-done.md`. Finish merge and deployment, attach results and evidence to the checklist, and request review. If checks fail, send corrective instructions to the active work session with `send_message_to_session`.
- When another card in `review` arrives, read its checklist results or the report on an older card and verify the evidence. If it passes, ask the user to confirm completion. Otherwise, leave a comment explaining what needs changing.
- Leave execution of a human-assigned card to its assignee. If the user requests a state change, use the authorized tools.

## Read cards

- Use the `cards` field from `get_folder(folder_id)` for a folder's cards, `list_cards(folder_id?, status?, query?)` for listing and search, and `get_card(card_id)` for one card. `search_cards(query, folder_id?, status?, limit?)` searches titles, numbers, status summaries, requests, handoffs, checklist items, notes, reports, and comments. It returns the source and excerpt of each match. `search_sessions` and `search_session_history` include the linked card's `card_id`, `card_number`, `card_title`, and `card_status`.
- When querying several cards or folders with the same tool and argument shape, try one representative query before running the rest. If validation fails, stop the batch and retest one query against the public tool definition.
- For more results, follow the returned cursor. Use `list_cards(all=true)` only when you need every card and omit `limit` and `cursor` in that call.
- Reuse the mutation response's version. Read the card again if you hit a conflict.

## Server and UI rules

Follow the section on card implementation in `soulstream-dev` when building or fixing a card feature. Assignee sessions follow the procedures in this skill.

See also `code-delegation.md`, `delegate-task`, `work-plan` for turning plans into cards, `long-term-plan.md` for plans across multiple cards, `verify-before-done.md`, and `ui-design`.

# UI design rules for tokens, components, spacing, and alignment

## When to use this skill

Use these rules to build UI or change typography, spacing, alignment, widths, or components in the web dashboard, Soul app, and published pages. Implementers read them before starting. Delegators and `review-code` reviewers read them before deciding. Follow `ui-visual-integrity.md` for screenshot verification.

These rules address recurring review issues with small text, inconsistent components, misalignment, and uneven margins and spacing.

## 0. Prerequisites for all UI work

These 18 requirements apply to every project with a visible interface, including Soulstream web and app screens, published pages, tools, and Slack blocks. Plan for them before implementation. For each one, report what you matched and how you checked it. Reviewers verify each one on the screen or render tree. A missing check blocks review.

1. **Text size.** Match the typography token of a nearby element with the same role. Use body sizing for body text, inputs, and buttons. An input that serves the same role as the chat composer uses the composer's token.
2. **Reuse components.** Use the existing row, card, bubble, input, cap button, sheet, or popover for the same role. When necessary, add a variant such as small or embedded to that component.
3. **Padding.** Inherit padding and gaps from the component. A crowded element often comes from cutting padding to reach a target height. Preserve each value that contributes to the height.
4. **Text position.** Vertically center text in single-line inputs and buttons. Start multiline inputs at one line and grow them as needed. Keep the first line vertically centered in the empty input. Vertically center elements placed on the same row.
5. **Scrollbars.** Use the project's treatment for scroll areas, such as thin overlay scrollbars that appear when needed. Preserve the page scrollbar and apply the project's styling. For published HTML, follow the scrollbar section in `html-make`.
6. **Focus outline.** Use the project's focus style, such as the one on the chat input, in place of the browser's square outline.
7. **Surfaces and opacity.** Use the material of an existing surface with the same role for sheets, panels, and chat messages. Keep glass surfaces consistent and give chat messages enough opacity for text to remain legible.
8. **Open and enlarge content.** Let users click images and attachments to enlarge or open them and click anywhere in a list row to activate it. Carry over the behavior available in chat.
9. **Copy and visual clarity.** Explain through diagrams, callouts, exploded views, highlights, interactive states, and layout hierarchy as appropriate. Apply three questions to every static or dynamic string, including headings, labels, instructions, empty states, errors, and tooltips. Is it necessary? Can you shorten it? If it cannot be shorter, can it be less prominent? Omit copy when users can already tell the state and find their next action. Include only the information they need.
10. **Start with the content.** Begin with the list, text, or input. Keep rows of summary tiles, selected values, or count cards out of the top of a page, including under a title, hero, or lead. Borders, surfaces, shadows, rules, and spacing all count as ways to make such a row. These rows repeat what the screen shows next. When numbers need to come first, use a conclusion sentence, chart, or table. A number can lead when it is the app's subject, such as current temperature or profiler response time. The Index preset's ledger rows are exempt when each number and claim share one line in a table of contents.
11. **Text selection.** Prevent selection by drag or double-click on controls such as buttons, tabs, menus, chips, toggles, toolbars, control bars, canvas overlays, sortable headers, and selectable rows. On app surfaces, apply this to UI framing text such as badges and input or section labels as well. Keep body text, code, errors, identifiers, and result values selectable. In apps, disable selection by default and enable it for content. In document pages, keep selection on by default and disable it on controls. When a clickable row contains document text, support drag selection without activating the row. Click and double-click should leave the text unselected. Use the project's selection policy file when present, such as `selection.css`.
12. **Alignment and margins.** Compare left and right edges, vertical centers, top edges of adjacent items, balanced padding, and spacing within and between groups in the screenshot. Assess right edges on elements with a visible boundary such as a box or rule. See sections 4, 5, and 11.
13. **Loading.** For first entry, navigation, tab switches, and data, 3D, or media loading, render the final layout frame first. Use the project's skeleton or progress treatment in the content slot. Keep bare "Loading" text out of unrelated positions such as the top left. Give users a visible loading state. Keep the layout steady as content loads, and show failures in the same slot. Delay the response and capture the loading state.

Checks 14–18 require interaction. A single screenshot misses many of these failures. Before requesting review, run the repository's visual review script (section 9) and record results in the screenshot folder's `operations.md`. Give a one-line reason for each check that does not apply.

14. **Focus after actions.** After clicking a button, menu, or tab, or opening or closing a dialog or sheet, put focus where the user will act next. On open, focus the first input or action. On close, return focus to the trigger. Keep focus from disappearing or jumping to the start of the page.
15. **Tab and Esc.** Make Tab follow the reading order and skip hidden or obscured elements. Esc closes the active dialog, sheet, popover, or menu and leaves the underlying screen alone.
16. **Overflow and clipping at minimum width.** Render long titles, names, and large numbers at the narrowest supported width, or 360px if unspecified. Keep the page free of horizontal scrolling. Wrap or truncate text without overlap or pushing buttons out. See sections 5 and 8.
17. **Errors.** If loading or an action fails, show the error and a way to retry in the loading slot (check 13). Give the user an actionable message. Force a failing response and capture the result.
18. **Resize.** Resize an open screen between wide and narrow widths. Check that layout adapts, popovers and menus stay anchored, and scroll position and typed text survive.

In delegation briefs, name the component to reuse and the content to replace. Specify constituent sizes and spacing and calculate the total. Send one current brief after incorporating corrections.

## 1. Use project tokens

- Use project tokens for font size, weight, line height, padding, gap, radius, and button size. Keep new literal pixel values out of these rules.
- Use the closest token if an exact one is missing. Report any need for a new token to the delegator.

See "Project token files", "Radius tokens", and "CSS checker" in `ui-css-recipes`, linked from section 15. They cover token names and the command, baseline, and enforcement for off-token values.

### Border radius

Web and app radii start from R=24.

1. Frames use R (24). This includes panels, panes, dialogs, the top of bottom sheets (0 at the bottom), popovers, menus, select popups, toasts, and tooltips. In the app, also apply it to glass backgrounds (`glassSoft`), modals, and cards and rows on the screen surface.
2. Pill shapes use half their height. Apply this to buttons, chips, badges, tabs, segments, switches, menu and select items, and avatars. Icon buttons are circular.
3. Nested elements use max(F, R - d), where F = R / 2 = 12 and d is the distance to the enclosing frame's edge. Apply this to cards, rows, message containers, inputs, select triggers, text boxes, navigation items, sticky notes (multiply by `--postit-scale` on web), code blocks, and images. The result is 20 at d=4, 16 at d=8, and 12 at d=12 or greater.
4. Fixed M = R / 6 = 4 applies to inline code, keyboard shortcuts (kbd), and checkboxes.
5. Chat messages use the same radius on all four corners and have no tails. The chat composer preserves half the single-line height as its radius, 24 on web and 28 on app, even as it grows. Keep native app sheets at 0.

Use the radius tokens from "Radius tokens" in `ui-css-recipes`.

## 2. Typography

- Choose the token by role: page title, section heading, card title, body, metadata, or badge. Web v3 uses `--v3-type-page`, `section`, `card`, `body`, `meta`, and `badge`. The app uses display, section, cardTitle, body, meta, and label.
- Use the body token for readable text, such as body text, button text, checklist items, and descriptions.
- Reserve the metadata token (12px on web, 13 on app) for timestamps, counts, sources, and short tab or section menu labels. Use the badge token only in badges. Keep text at or above those sizes.
- Use the same token for the same role across screens. Match a new list item's type to the standard component next to it, such as a session card.

## 3. Components

- Reuse standard components for the same role. Examples include icon buttons (`DashboardIconCap` on web), section headings, card frames, context menus, and dialogs. Find the component before starting and name it in the report.
- If the existing component needs a variation, propose a variant to the delegator. Avoid copying a component to make a near duplicate.
- Use the same button size and shape in a row. Keep text and icon buttons in separate rows.
- Apply project styles to focus outlines, scrollbars, and textarea resize handles.
- Limit nested borders to two layers. Use spacing to show boundaries and dividers only when spacing is insufficient.

## 4. Spacing

- Choose values on the spacing scale, from `--v3-space-1` through `--v3-space-8` on web.
- Use one spacing value per level on a screen. Give panel side padding, section gaps, heading-to-content gaps, and gaps between cards each their own consistent value.
- Increase gaps as the level rises. Gaps inside cards are smaller than gaps between cards, which are smaller than gaps between sections.

## 5. Alignment and width

- Use one left and one right edge per screen. Align the first header control, title, section headings, cards, and side menu to the left edge. Align the last header control and cards to the right edge.
- Align adjacent columns, such as sidebar and content or two panels, at the top.
- Match heights and vertically center elements on a row, such as chips and buttons or icons and text.
- Fill the rectangular space inside rounded panel borders. Use a centered max-width only where the design calls for it, such as a readable line length for long text.
- Ellipsize variable-length text such as titles, descriptions, and chips. Prevent clipping and overlap.

## 6. Reuse the layout across entry points

- Share markup and sizing when the same screen opens inline and in an overlay. Let only the outer frame, such as glass borders or dividers, depend on the entry point.
- Keep the structure and order aligned when a screen exists on web and app.
- Use the existing screen frame for new screens and replace the content. Inherit width, spacing, scrolling, and header and composer placement. Specify different structure only where needed in the mockup.
- Begin the mockup without copy. Add text users need to understand the state or find their next action. Shorten it and reduce its prominence in the order described in check 9.

## 7. Keep layout changes within scope

- Check what a shared class or token affects before editing it. Use screen-specific classes for screen-specific needs. Fix a recurring inconsistency at its shared owner and review the relevant call sites together. Avoid per-screen CSS workarounds for shared defects.
- Compare before and after screenshots of at least one other screen that shares the changed value to verify that its layout stays the same.

## 8. Verify layout relationships

Check how sizes combine in the render. Use coordinates on web and the render tree and combined styles on app. Values such as a 44px button, a 56px row, or a matching `minHeight` alone cannot establish layout correctness.

Describe mockups and delegation briefs the same way. Specify avatar size, line height, padding, and gaps, then calculate the total. If you inherit a component's frame, tell the implementer what it must match and how to verify it.

| Target | Relationship to verify |
| --- | --- |
| List row | Content and padding determine its natural height. The top and bottom look balanced. Keep the padding consistent when the row's height changes. |
| Composer | Growing text leaves the selected chip and send button at their own sizes. |
| Narrow screen | Long chips shrink or wrap and the send button stays in place. |
| Detail panel | Opening an adjacent panel, such as Sessions, preserves the main content's position and width. |
| Shared component | When the default size is too large, use the shared compact variant. |
| Indentation and spacing | Parent padding and child margins add up to the single intended value. |

Cover states the user often encounters and states where the layout has failed.

## 9. Report results and keep visual checks in the repository

Keep screenshot and layout measurement scripts in the repository, outside `.local/tmp/`. For example, use `scripts/visual-check/` or `tests/visual/`. Maintain them like unit or end-to-end tests.

- Implementers run the repository's visual review script when creating or changing a screen. Update and commit it for new screens or scenarios such as wide or narrow viewports, loading, empty states, or errors.
- Delegators and reviewers use the same checked-in script or inspect its outputs. This lets them focus on the visual decision.

A visual review script needs assertions that detect the defect.

- Run a new assertion once against the code before the fix and confirm that it fails. An existing `role=dialog` or the absence of an element that never rendered proves nothing about the fix.
- Check overflow beyond `scrollWidth`. Measure text collapsing to zero width, overflow to the left, clipping without ellipsis, and dates or numbers breaking across lines (`getClientRects().length`). A check such as "width is greater than zero" is too weak.
- Test demanding data and states. Include the longest allowed titles and names, the narrowest width, and loading, error, empty, and disabled states.
- Measure color and contrast from screenshot pixels. Transparency and glass can change what users see from computed styles.

Include the following in the UI work report.

- Components and tokens reused, plus any new pixel values. Write "None" when there are no new pixel values.
- The path and command for the visual script you ran or updated.
- Before and after screenshot paths for wide and narrow viewports with production-shaped data.
- Loading screenshots for screens that wait for content (check 13).
- Results of interaction checks 14–18 from the repository's visual script. Write them in the screenshot folder's `operations.md` and give its path in the report. The delegator sends this file to the reviewer too. Include:
  - An "Items 14–18" table with the check number, pass or not applicable, and one line of evidence or reason.
  - A "Dialogs and inline editing" table with one row per dialog, sheet, popover, menu, or inline edit. Give the target, how to open it, initial focus, Enter and Esc behavior, and focus after closing. Write "None" if no such target changed.
  - The command and artifact paths.
- For corrections after review, the path to the interaction scenario added to the repository script.
- Edge and top alignment coordinates from getBoundingClientRect, with no more than 1px difference. Use the coordinates to support a direct comparison and write what you see. See `ui-visual-integrity.md` section 2.
- Results of screenshot comparisons for screens that should look the same.
- A list of the copy on screen and which step of check 9 it passed. Include copy removed, shortened, or made less prominent.

## 10. Use the Soulstream component review window

- Use only components present in the component review window. On web and app, consult the implementation in that platform's own review window.
- This requirement covers variants, combinations, layouts, and responsive configurations as well as individual components. A registered component alone does not authorize a new composition.
- If you need a configuration missing from the review window, show the user the requirement the existing configurations cannot meet. Present the difference with a concrete mockup and comparison material. Obtain the user's consent before implementing or using it. Approval from a delegator or review agent cannot substitute.
- General feature work does not grant consent to an unregistered configuration. An explicit request or approval in the current conversation covers that configuration, so use it without asking again.
- Mark user-review mockups as proposals and keep them disconnected from the live UI. Adding the configuration to the review window before or during the same PR does not establish consent.
- Add an approved configuration to the review window as a real implementation sample. Verify it with the same props, widths, states, and affiliation data as production. Use the actual implementation in the sample.
- Reviewers compare production components and layouts with the review window and check evidence of required user consent. Keep unregistered or unapproved configurations out of production, merge, and deployment.
- Restoring an approved layout after an unauthorized placement error uses an existing configuration. Treat the approved layout as the reference for new screens.
- Verify web and app in their own environments.

## 11. Fix recurring problems in the shared layout

- Give elements with the same role the same shape and sizing rules. Changing an icon, action, or state color should preserve button size, baseline, and internal spacing. Preserve surfaces, radii, and text edges when switching from reading to editing.
- Match the outer left and right insets and keep space within a group smaller than between groups. Choose horizontal and vertical padding for the layout. Compare the spaces beside avatars, between titles and affiliations, and between titles and the next item.
- Give each spacing value one owner. The frame owns outer insets and column gaps, the action group owns its inner gaps, and each button owns its size. Check for unwanted sums of parent padding, child margins, and action padding. Set same-role button sizes in the shared role so each state-specific caller does not pick its own size.
- Verify shared component reuse and consistency of the final render separately. Record mismatches found in existing implementations for correction.
- Compare states and call sites side by side with the same content and width. Start with combinations that have failed, such as a list and folder, default and completed, two and three lines, and read and edit. Include real call sites as well as the review page.
- Distinguish DOM boundaries from visible text and shapes. Matching padding can still look unbalanced because of line height, an empty row, or minimum button height. Use measurements to support a judgment about balance and grouping on comparison screenshots.
- Report the shared cause, where the fix lives, which caller exceptions you removed, and how the states compare. Add only the shared structure needed to remove the cause.

## 12. Review screenshots and interactions

After opening a UI PR, inspect actual screenshots and interaction results. Review the visual result, use of shared components and tokens, common and exceptional paths, and the experience on web and app. A failed check blocks approval. Use test results and measurements alongside direct review.

## 13. Consult the ui-practice catalog

The shared `ui-practice` catalog covers layout and spacing as well as behavior for individual controls. Its branches are layout-spacing, text-copy, scroll-overflow, states-feedback, interaction-platform, controls-input, controls-action, and collections-media. Each has criteria from real cases and sources for public guidance. Read the relevant branches before implementing or reviewing. If `work-plan-execute`, `review-code`, `soulstream-mockup`, or `html-make` did not expand the branch, use `match_skill_catalogs(intent)` in place of `load_skill` and read it by node_id from the branch table. To see the root and branch list, call `compile_subtree(node_id="{{node_id:catalog.ui_practice.body}}", depth=1, titles_only=true)`. Follow this document when the catalog differs.

## 14. Use modern-web-guidance for implementation

The Chrome team's implementation guide covers how to implement these rules and `ui-practice` in HTML, CSS, and browser JavaScript, including fallbacks. Consult it before writing web UI code. Reviewers use this document and the catalog for acceptance criteria. Their rules take precedence.

```link
call: modern-web-guidance
when: Before writing web UI code in HTML, CSS, or browser JavaScript
```

## 15. Prevent recurring CSS defects

Read `ui-css-recipes` before writing CSS for a web screen. It groups recurring review findings by cause and includes patterns, project token files, radius tokens, and the CSS checker.

```link
call: ui-css-recipes
when: Before writing or editing web UI CSS, including plain CSS, CSS modules, and Tailwind classes, or when looking up token files, radius tokens, or the CSS checker
```

Use the repository's visual checks, such as Playwright scripts, for requirements the CSS checker cannot measure.

- Use a minimum of 13px for all text. Set a floor on relative sizing such as `em`, for example `max(var(--meta-token), 0.85em)`.
- Use tokens at 4px intervals for spacing. Move off-scale values to the nearest interval. If the difference exceeds 4px, preserve the value with a token sum in `calc()`.
- Use `word-break: keep-all` for Korean text, including in table cells, so titles, outlines, and product names wrap at word boundaries when they fit. Use `word-break: normal` for English, Japanese, and Chinese. For Japanese, you can use `word-break: auto-phrase` where supported. Apply `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to all languages.
- Prevent horizontal overflow and text clipping by an `overflow: hidden` ancestor. Keep single-line buttons, badges, and toolbars on one line.
- For changes to appearance, run the repository's visual checks at wide and narrow widths (minimum 360px) and in light and dark themes. Add an assertion for defects found during review and verify it fails on the commit before the fix.
