skill.statechart.body.title: SKILL.md
skill.statechart.body.content:
# statechart

Use statecharts to describe, visualize, and check state rules in systems with concurrent state, such as Soulstream cards, sessions, and deployment flows. The XState definition in product code is the source of truth. Generate diagrams from it. Draw by hand only during analysis or early design, before a definition exists.

Show nested states and transitions. A few named states rarely describe all the configurations the code can reach. Look for missing hierarchy, unnamed states, and interactions between regions.

## When to use it

- The same state condition appears in several places, or answering "What happens if this event occurs in this state?" requires reading several files.
- A PR changes state rules. Attach the generated diagrams to the PR and card when you submit or review it.
- A defect needs a path through states to explain it.
- Use a simpler diagram for a branch within one function, a linear flow, or an architecture overview.

Use exhaustive traversal when each state change happens in a single step inside a transaction that locks one row. This gives the equivalent of TLC's check for these machines. The comparison tests in section 5 catch differences between a handwritten model and running code. For small machines, reading the code gives at least as much insight as a separate TLA+ model. Skip TLA+ for this workflow.

## 1. Identify the actual state

Start with what changes independently.

1. **Divide into regions.** A region can be any value the system remembers, even when there is no dedicated field. A card has regions for card status, open questions, scheduled wake, and assignee.
2. **Derive outputs.** Calculate a value with no memory of its own from the current configuration. For example, derive a card's board entry. Making it a region would add rules that read the other regions again.
3. **Find parent states.** A condition repeated in two or more places suggests an unnamed parent state. For example, `status in (on_hold, done, cancelled)` means "Off the board". A use of the parent condition that checks only one child state may be a defect.
4. **Name implicit states.** Look for behavior changes with no state name, such as "Usage blocked with a wake scheduled". Look where code compares literal prose, recounts another table, or changes only the status summary.
5. **Keep permissions and records separate.** Put who can do what in a permissions table. Keep an individual question's lifecycle on its record. Track only whether an open question exists in the region.
6. **Count configurations.** Count named states, reachable configurations, and configurations distinguishable by stored fields alone. A large difference is a reason to use a statechart.

## 2. Draw the chart

- **Hierarchy.** Draw a shared outgoing transition once from the parent state. Use one parent transition for a person moving a card to any state. Put shared entry and exit actions on the parent. A shared action present on only one child suggests a defect. In section 3, reopening restores question entries only from On hold.
- **Parallel regions.** Separate regions with `--`. Show their interactions using transition guards such as `[when a question is open]` and actions such as `/ clear the scheduled wake`. Examine these interactions closely.
- **Labels.** Use what the reader experiences, such as "The user replies" or "Wake when the limit resets". Keep variable, function, and event identifiers out of visible labels. Combine events with the same result on one arrow under a shared label. Use the other region's state name in brackets when it supplies the guard.
- **Defect marks.** Mark a state that breaks an invariant with `breaks` (red). Use `mayBreak` (orange) when only some configurations in the state break it. Use `bugPath` on the shortest path to a defect. In the legend or handoff, name each state and the invariant it breaks. Keep states that break different invariants distinct.
- **Size.** Make one overview for parent states, regions, and interactions, plus three to five detailed diagrams by parent state or region. Aim for about 20 transitions per diagram. Combine states that behave identically. If needed, hide redundant arrows such as a return available in every state. Keep all these properties.
  - Every state remains reachable from the start.
  - Every state with an outgoing path still shows at least one outgoing arrow.
  - Show or hide all events on an arrow together. List what you hid in the handoff.
- **Direction.** Use `direction TB` to stack regions vertically. Diagrams much wider than 2000px are difficult to read at normal zoom.

## 3. Write and render Mermaid

Use Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2` for analysis before the definition exists and for generated output. Use English IDs and show labels with `ID: Label` or `state "Label" as ID`.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    direction TB
    classDef breaks fill:#ffecee,stroke:#e72e3b
    state "One card" as Card {
        state "Card status" as Status {
            state "On the board" as On {
                Running: Running
                Asked: Blocked on a question
                Running --> Asked: Ask a question
                Asked --> Running: The user replies
            }
            state "Off the board" as Off {
                Hold: On hold
                Done: Done
            }
            On --> Off: Remove the card / Remove its board entry
            Off --> On: Reopen / Restore question entries [only from On hold] (어긋남 7)
        }
        --
        state "Scheduled wake" as Resv {
            NoResv: No scheduled wake
            Wake: Wake when the limit resets
            NoResv --> Wake: A short usage limit ends the assignee session
            Wake --> NoResv: Leave the usage-blocked state
            Wake --> Wake: Keep the wake when the assignee changes (어긋남 2)
        }
    }
    class Off breaks
    class Wake breaks
```

Render with Pele. On first run, the script downloads `pele@1.9.0` into `~/.cache/statechart-pele` and embeds the light and dark styles from `assets/statechart.css` in the SVG.

Open the PNG and check that each state is in the intended box.

- An arrow from a parent block to a child can pull the child out of its declared box. Put arrows between children in the block that declares them. Connect parent states for cross-level transitions.
- Pele always lays out `--` regions horizontally. With three or more regions, use two columns and stack the remaining regions inside the second column as separate parent boxes.
- Pele cannot color arrows individually. Append the renderer marker `(어긋남 N)` to defect transition labels and mark the destination state.
- Pele ignores Mermaid's `theme` setting. Set colors in the CSS file.

## 4. Generate diagrams from XState v5

- Define hierarchy, `type: "parallel"`, events, named guards, and actions with `setup` and `createMachine`.
- Use the pure `transition(machine, snapshot, event)` function. It returns the next snapshot and actions.
- Build the snapshot from persisted fields with `machine.resolveState({ value })`.
- Traverse configurations with `xstate/graph`.
- Keep persisted fields as the source of truth. Avoid a running `createActor` instance, persisting the whole snapshot, and external visualization in Stately.
- Inside the transaction that locks the row, use `resolveState` on the fields, call `transition` with the event, and write the resulting fields. Run returned actions after commit.
- Define readable labels alongside the definition. Use the state `description` and a display-name table for events, guards, and actions. The generator uses these labels. Put each transition explanation in one place for the diagram and rule document. Fail generation on a transition without an explanation.

### Decision machine structure

Start with this structure from Soulstream's card rules when modeling another system.

- **Regions.** Read stored fields into parallel regions (status, open questions, scheduled wake, assignee, and archive for cards). Use a verdict region to choose from ordered rejection transitions, no change, and acceptance.
- **Symbolic actions.** Define actions as symbols of write intent. The service asks for one verdict and passes only the final writes from the decoder to persistence. Persistence applies SQL fences and updates numbers, version, and audit fields. Keep decisions such as clearing another field on a state change in the machine so there is one policy.
- **Entry table.** Put rejections that depend only on actor type in one entry table. Check it before taking the lock. Keep each rule in that table or the machine as appropriate.
- **Evidence stages.** Stage reads that require a lock or are expensive. The machine returns `needsEvidence` just before the first guard that needs the stage. The service evaluates, reads only that stage, and evaluates again. Earlier rejections still skip unnecessary reads and locks. A `needsEvidence` response yields neither a write nor an error.
- **Fences as values.** Pass SQL fence results to the machine as evidence. The formatter emits the existing error text and code.
- **Commands as events.** Model a helper that only runs inside other commands, such as claiming assignment, as an effect of those commands. Give every machine event a runtime call site.

### Soulstream generator

- `orch-server-ts/src/statechart/mermaid.ts` takes a machine and view definitions and emits Mermaid. Each view selects regions and events. List hidden events in the source table below the diagram. Split the view if a diagram would exceed 25 arrows.
- `orch-server-ts/src/cards/state/card_charts.ts` defines the card views. It produces:
  - `docs/cards/card-state.md` with state and storage tables, permissions by actor relationship, rules and production call sites, evidence stages, and invariants and gaps.
  - `docs/cards/generated` with a `.mmd`, rendered `.svg` and `.png` for each view, and `promises.json`.
- Regenerate with `corepack pnpm@10.32.1 --dir orch-server-ts exec tsx scripts/card-state-charts.ts docs/cards/generated`. If a `.mmd` changes, also render the `.svg` and `.png` as in section 3.
- `tests/card-state-charts.test.ts` fails when generated artifacts differ from the definition. `tests/card-machine-inventory.test.ts` fails when a machine event has no runtime call site or SQL that writes cards is outside the allowlist. Include the updated definition and regenerated artifacts in the same state-rule PR.
- For systems without a definition, such as session lifecycle or deployment flow, sketch with sections 1–3 first. Use the same machine structure and generator when moving to code.

## 5. Check for gaps

1. **Write invariants as functions.** Take a configuration and return a Boolean. For example, "An open question has a board entry" or "A usage-blocked card has a scheduled wake". Preserve the invariant even when the check fails.
2. **Traverse all reachable configurations.** Get them with `getAdjacencyMap` and check the invariants. Mark violations with `breaks` or `mayBreak`. Mark shortest paths from `getShortestPaths` with `bugPath`.
3. **Check for stalls.** Every reachable configuration needs a user-visible indication, such as a board entry, or an exit triggered by time. A configuration with neither can stall unnoticed.
4. **Compare with the real service.**
   - Extract event paths with `getShortestPaths`, `getSimplePaths`, and `createTestModel`.
   - Replay one step at a time through the actual service and a test database. Compare the resulting fields to the machine's configuration.
   - If a path cannot be reproduced in the service, check the model first.
   - When moving existing code to a machine, capture the old service's observations once as a fixture. Require both the new service's replay and the pure machine's predictions to match. Preserve the original fixture so changed behavior cannot become the new baseline.
   - Keep behavior changes out of the structure migration PR. Run the base commit's actual methods to establish expected results where behavior could differ. Replace tests that fix temporary migration machinery with tests of the final contract and carry over their behavioral expectations.
5. **Run on each state-rule PR.** Repeat steps 2 and 3 and attach the generated diagrams.

The machine treats one event as one step. Check multistep paths outside the transaction separately, such as reading, sending a message, and writing again. Confirm that the final write rechecks the conditions.

## 6. Present the diagrams

Keep one `.mmd` source and present it in the format appropriate to each use.

| Use | Output |
| --- | --- |
| Card evidence, PRs, and review | Light and dark PNGs from Pele |
| Overviews, details, and before-and-after figures in reports and published documents (`html-make`) | A `statechart` block in diagram-autolayout |
| Clickable state details | An html-diagram page |

**Published figures.** Give diagram-autolayout the Mermaid from section 3, either as a `.mmd` file or pasted into a `statechart` block in the Markdown draft. It renders nested parent states, parallel regions (`--`), start and end states (`[*]`), self-loops, and defect marks (`breaks`, `mayBreak`, `bugPath`). Colors use the selected document preset's (Index, Apple, Astryx) tokens. A label ending in `(어긋남 N)` gets a bold red marker. Include the legend required in section 2 and name both the color and state. The figure distinguishes the two defect marks by color alone.

The document renderer differs from Pele in four ways.

- Parallel regions stack when they exceed a document column. A cross-level transition connects the nearest parent states and reports `! L<line>`. Still write the source according to section 3 so it works in Pele.
- Labels use document body sizing, roughly 17px for state names, so output is larger. Use `manifest.json`'s `width` to check fit (920px in Index). If too wide, split by region or parent state using the statechart block rules in diagram-autolayout. An oversized diagram scrolls horizontally. Use at most one.
- Put `title:` in a document heading or caption. The renderer leaves it out of the figure.
- The renderer accepts no notes, forks and joins, choice states, or history states.

**Show a fix before and after.** Take the fragment that contains the defect and put it in a `statechart` block. Prefix changed lines with `+ ` or `- ` to show additions and removals in one figure. Use `~ ` only on states and parent states. It is an error on a transition. Removed lines and borders fade and their text is struck through but stays readable. Keep the parent boxes and region names so readers can place the fragment in the full diagram. For a label or guard change, mark the old line with `-` and the new one with `+`. Keep marked-up lines in diagram-autolayout only and use unmarked source with Pele.

```statechart
stateDiagram-v2
    direction TB
    state "Region 1. Card status" as Status {
        state "On the board" as On
        state "Off the board" as Off {
            Hold: On hold
            Done: Done
            Cancelled: Canceled
        }
        On --> Off: Remove the card / Remove all board entries
        - Off --> On: Restore the card / Restore question entries [only from On hold] (어긋남 7)
        + Off --> On: Restore the card / Restore question entries [from any Off the board state]
    }
```

**Interactive exploration.** When the user selects a state, show incoming and outgoing events, guards, and actions, the code location, and the defect explanation. Use regions as path filters so the user can explore what happens in a state.

## 7. Hand off the result

Include the PNG and `.mmd` source, one line per defect with the violated invariant in reader-facing words and the path that breaks it, any model omissions or hidden arrows, and the regeneration command. Attach the PNG as checklist evidence on a card.

## Source

The reader-facing labels, guards in brackets, size of about 20 transitions, rules for merging and hiding transitions, `breaks` and `mayBreak` marks, path replay against real code, and colors come from pstack's statechart skill (MIT, Lauren Tan), adapted for XState. The adaptation omits pstack's TLA+ pipeline. See `NOTICE.md`.

skill.ui_css_recipes.body.content:
# CSS patterns that prevent recurring defects

These patterns address recurring causes of UI and UX review findings. Replace sample tokens with the project tokens below. Class names are illustrative. Reuse an existing component with the same role when it already uses the pattern. See `ui-design` section 3.

## Project token files

| Project | Token source |
| --- | --- |
| Soulstream web v3 | `--v3-type-*`, `--v3-space-*`, `--v3-action-size`, and `--v3-control-height` in `unified-dashboard/client/v3/v3-visual-system.css`. See "Border radius" in `ui-design` and "Radius tokens" below. |
| Soul app | Typography and spacing in `src/theme/tokens.ts`. See "Border radius" in `ui-design` and "Radius tokens" below. |
| Published HTML bundle (html-publish document model renderer) | `--fs-*`, `--sp-*`, `--r-*`, and color in the shared `skills/html-publish/templates/tokens.css`. |
| Standalone published HTML (html-make) | Text tokens from the selected preset's design system card and static HTML sample (Index, Apple, or Astryx). Find both in the shared html-design-preset catalog expanded by html-make. See "Typography" in `html-make` for the default and minimum body sizes. |

## Radius tokens

Follow "Border radius" in `ui-design` section 1 to choose a radius for each element. Use these tokens.

- The web source is `packages/soul-ui/src/styles/globals.css`. Use `--radius-root`, `--radius-floor`, `--radius-mark`, `--radius-pill` on `:root`, and the concentric utility `rounded-in-N`.
- Use only `rounded-root`, `rounded-floor`, `rounded-mark`, `rounded-full`, `rounded-none`, and `rounded-in-N` as Tailwind radius classes.
- The class merger (`cn`) recognizes these as radius classes and keeps one.
- `soul-desktop/src/index.css` mirrors the web values.
- The app source is `soul-app/src/theme/tokens.ts`. Use `ROOT_RADIUS`, `FLOOR_RADIUS`, `MARK_RADIUS`, `CAPSULE_RADIUS`, `concentricRadius(inset)`, and `capsuleRadius(height)`.

## CSS checker

Soulstream web and frontend projects enforce the token and radius rules from `ui-design` section 1. Frontend projects use an exact copy of Soulstream's `scripts/check-ui-css.mjs` with all eight rules enabled. For each file, it counts color literals, font size and font family literals, radius literals, spacing literals, `user-select` outside the policy file, `outline: none`, and the Tailwind arbitrary values `text-[..]` and `rounded-[..]`. Counts above the baseline in `scripts/ui-css-baseline.json` fail.

- Run `node scripts/check-ui-css.mjs` at the repository root. For published HTML bundles, run `node skills/html-publish/scripts/check-ui-css.mjs` at the shared files root.
- CI runs the check in Soulstream and other main repositories. Failures identify the line and a replacement token. Replace new literal values with tokens. If counts drop, run with `--update` to lower the baseline. If a value must stay, adjust the count by hand and explain the reason in the PR.
- Start new repositories, templates, and presets with the same checker, all eight rules enabled, and a baseline of zero. Explain any disabled rule or raised baseline in the PR.

## Overflow and truncation

```css
/* Flex and grid children default to min-width: auto. Set the text area's minimum to zero so it can shrink. */
.row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: var(--space-2); }
.row > .text { flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }
.row > .action { flex: none; }                 /* Keep the button at its size and in view. */
.grid > * { min-width: 0; }

.prose { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }            /* Long URLs and identifiers can wrap within the cell. */
.nobr { white-space: nowrap; }                 /* Keep date and time, numbers and units, and code chips together. */
```

- If a text area collapses to 10px or zero, check for missing `min-width: 0` or a neighboring element that needs `flex: none`.
- `overflow: hidden` can clip shadows and focus rings. Add inner space or draw the ring inside when it clips.
- Let narrow layouts stack vertically. Avoid fixed minimum widths such as `min-width: 1800px`.
- Use `word-break: keep-all` on Korean body text and keep it in Korean table cells. Use `word-break: normal` for English, Japanese, and Chinese. For Japanese, you can use `word-break: auto-phrase` where supported. Apply `overflow-wrap: anywhere` to all languages.
- For a long token such as a file path, insert `<wbr>` after each `/` so readers can see the end. Break within a token only if it exceeds the cell width.

## Give spacing one owner

```css
/* The parent's gap sets sibling spacing. Child margins can add another 24 and make 48. */
.stack { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--space-3); }
.stack > * { margin: 0; }

.panel { padding: var(--space-4); }            /* Keep padding on the top and bottom as well as the sides. */

/* A scroll area without bottom padding can clip the last item's shadow and focus ring. */
.scroll-area { padding-block-end: var(--space-4); scroll-padding-block-end: var(--space-4); }
```

- Choose spacing tokens and reuse the common class neighboring rows use. Keep values like a 6px or 8px dot consistent with adjacent elements.
- Sibling gaps like 26.5px and 16px at one level indicate mixed margins. Use a flex or grid gap for the list.

## Put text selection in the policy file

```css
/* App screens disable selection by default and enable it on readable content. */
.app-shell { -webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none; }
.app-shell :is(.message-body, pre, code, .error-text, .identifier, .result-value) { -webkit-user-select: text; user-select: text; }

/* Document pages leave selection enabled by default and disable it on controls. */
:is(button, [role="button"], [role="tab"], summary, label, .chip, th[aria-sort]) { -webkit-user-select: none; user-select: none; }
```

- Declare `user-select` only in the project policy file. Soulstream uses `v3-selection-policy.css`, published HTML bundles use `templates/selection.css`, and html-make uses one `<style data-ui="selection">` block. Add selectors there for new elements. Component-level declarations fail the CI check.
- Give the rule enabling selection enough specificity to win. A selector wrapped in `:where()` has zero specificity.

## Focus indication

```css
/* When removing the outline, include the project's replacement focus style in the same group. */
.control:focus { outline: none; }
.control:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: inherit; }

/* A frame with overflow: hidden clips the ring. Draw it inside or add room in the frame. */
.clipped .control:focus-visible { outline-offset: -2px; }
```

- Use the shared button component. A bare `<button>` lacks the project's focus style.
- Match the focus ring to the element with `border-radius: inherit`.
- Test where focus goes by interacting with the UI. See `ui-design` section 0, checks 14 and 15.

## Use one typography token for each role

```css
.card-action { font: var(--v3-type-body); }    /* The token sets size, weight, and line height together. */
button, input, textarea, select { font: inherit; }   /* Inherit the project's font in form controls instead of showing the 16px default. */
```

- Include `input`, `textarea`, and `select` when targeting input controls.
- If a rule overrides `font`, apply the role's token at that rule.
- Avoid forcing monospace on prose that can include CJK text, including Korean. Use tokens for text size and keep size out of inline `style`.

## Keep layout steady across states

```css
.header { min-block-size: var(--control-height); }   /* Keep the header height when a button arrives late. */
.slot[aria-busy="true"] { min-block-size: var(--row-height); }   /* Reserve the final content height while loading. */

/* Style disabled and aria-disabled together so both keep the dimmed appearance. */
:is(button, [role="button"]):is(:disabled, [aria-disabled="true"]) { opacity: var(--disabled-opacity); cursor: default; }

/* Set the selected state attribute and style it. */
:is([aria-current="page"], [aria-selected="true"]) { background: var(--surface-selected); }
```

- Use the same slot for loading and failure. Show one spinner or message at a time.

## Alignment

```css
.card { text-align: start; }                   /* Keep content start-aligned inside a centered ancestor. */
.toolbar { display: flex; align-items: center; }   /* Use the same size variant for controls on one row. A 32px input and 28px button do not match. */
.column > .item { align-self: start; }
```

## Color and radius

```css
.chip { color: var(--text-secondary); background: var(--surface-2); border-radius: var(--radius-small); }
.inner { border-radius: calc(var(--radius-window) - var(--space-2)); }   /* Inner radius equals outer radius minus the inset. */
```

- Use color tokens in place of hex or `rgb()` literals. Read the CSS token if JavaScript needs the value.
- Use the project's secondary text token. Dimming text with opacity can reduce contrast on glass.
- Use the project's placement and stacking order for fixed toasts and banners. Keep controls unobstructed.

Use `ui-design` as the source of truth when these recipes differ from it.
